title: A finished client-facing action plan with a working Approve button is rendered on no page, while the explicitly internal list is shown instead
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → "What we're fixing" (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: The client sees the internal engineering gap list. The polished plan they were designed to see — plain-English actions with an Approve button on each row that actually saves and posts to the activity timeline the team watches — is not on any screen in the product.
whyItsWrong: The data layer marks the gap array as internal and says in so many words to use the recommendations array for the client view. The panel does the opposite: it renders the gap array to clients and never reads the recommendations array, which is computed and persisted on every run. The client-facing component is complete and imported by zero files. Behind it, the approve action is real and authorized (a client can call it for their own account), the Firestore transaction is real, and approvals are deliberately preserved across re-captures. So the one place in this report where a client could act — and the one thing that would make the recommendation cards non-inert — is fully built, wired end to end, and invisible; and what they get instead is the data the codebase says never to show them. Git history sharpens this: the mounted version SHIPPED on 22 Jul (db573d0, the v1 QA sign-off) and was reverted hours later by the merge resolution in de0d414 — see finding 152. Restoring it is a revert-of-a-revert, not new work.

title: Card bodies are raw audit-model prose, and "What good looks like" just repeats the card title
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → "What we're fixing" → expanded card (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: Card titles read like an engineer's checklist: "LCP p75 under 2.5s", "INP p75 under 200ms", "Entity density about 15 recognized entities per 1000 words (no stuffing)", "At least 3 question-form subheadings with answers under 80 words". Expand one and the "what we found" line is whatever sentence the audit model happened to write that run ("robots.txt, fetched today, has no Disallow for ClaudeBot"). The "what good looks like" line then prints the exact same words as the card title you just clicked.
whyItsWrong: Three breaches of the house rule that clients never see raw model copy. (a) The found line and the extra evidence line are both the audit model's free-text evidence string, passed through the sanitizer with no normalization and straight into the page. (b) The benchmark is set to the registry label — the same string used as the title — so for every site-check card the goal line is a guaranteed duplicate; the presenter de-dupes the evidence line against the found line but nobody de-duped benchmark against title. (c) If the model emits an id that isn't in the registry, the model's own label becomes the client-facing card title. Polished plain-English copy for exactly these ids already exists in the codebase ("Tighten your page titles", "Add a short answer at the top of each guide") and this panel never touches it. The panel's own header comment claims everything a client reads is plain English by construction; the presenter's unit test explicitly exempts these passthrough fields from its leak check.

title: Cards promise Karos will apply the fix "automatically" — no such code path exists and there is nothing to press

whatYouSee: Expand almost any site-check card and the last line reads "Karos can apply this fix for you automatically." There is nothing to click. Nothing happens. Nothing is scheduled. The sentence just sits there as static text.
whyItsWrong: The agent-direct route is the default for every check bucket except off-site entity and index reach, so this sentence is on the majority of cards in the report. Nothing in the portal can apply a fix to a client's website: there is no apply action, no job type, and no writer for the gap record's generated-fix artifact field — the two producers hardcode it to null and nothing else ever sets it. So the most common sentence in the section promises an automation that does not exist, on the client's own dashboard, where a client will reasonably wait for a fix that no code will perform.

title: No "What we're fixing" card can hand off to an agent — the one link built for it can never render

whatYouSee: You expand any recommendation card. You get three text blocks — what we found, what good looks like, how it gets fixed — and then nothing. title: The headline AI-visibility score uses a different question set from every number below it, and it can never reach zero
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → score tiles and the engine comparison card (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: The tile reads "AI visibility today" with a non-zero grade, and its explainer says this is the number the fixes below are designed to move. Open the by-engine breakdown and ChatGPT shows a positive percentage. Scroll one card down to the ChatGPT card and it says no brands were named in ChatGPT's answers this run, share of conversation zero percent, cited as a source zero of fourteen answers, answered first zero of fourteen. A brand with no measured presence still shows a grade.
whyItsWrong: Two defects compound. First, mixed denominators: the headline index is deliberately fed the full question set — including the brand and navigational questions that name the client and are near-guaranteed hits — while every card, stat and gap below uses the category-only sub-metrics. So the tile and its by-engine breakdown can show a positive number next to a card of zeros, and the tile's claim that the fixes below move this number is false, because those fixes are derived from the category metrics. The same mismatch hits the "linked but not named" chip, which reads the full-set figure while the "cited as a source" line beside it in the same card is category-only. Second, a hardcoded floor: the per-engine score gives ten percent of its weight to a sentiment term, and sentiment is zero when the brand was never mentioned, which maps to the neutral midpoint and awards five points out of a hundred for having no presence at all. That contradicts this file's own rule, stated three times, that the estimated sentiment signal never enters a grade.

fix: Pick one denominator and state it. Either compute the headline index from `e.category` in src/lib/seo-geo.ts engineVisibilityScore (line 446) / computeVisibilityIndex (line 479) so the tile and the cards agree, or keep the full-set index for parity with the lab reference and change the tile explainer at src/components/seo-geo/presenter.ts:159 to say it includes the questions that name you, plus a second line showing the category-only figure the fixes actually move. Separately: drop the sentiment term from engineVisibilityScore (src/lib/seo-geo.ts:452) to honour the documented grade rule, or gate it on `mentionRate > 0` so zero presence scores zero. And switch the ghost chip at presenter.ts:457-459 from `row.` to `cat.` so it shares its card's denominator.

title: The same problem appears as two cards with contradictory priority chips
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → "What we're fixing" (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: Two cards about your sitemap: "Valid XML sitemap, referenced in robots.txt, no noindexed entries" and "Sitemap valid + referenced" — the same finding, tagged at different priorities. Two cards about your update dates, one tagged important and one tagged urgent. Two cards about indexability, two about scannable sections, two about headline structure. This duplication is a large part of why the list needs a "show all" toggle.
whyItsWrong: Nine check ids (BOTH-01, BOTH-02, BOTH-03, BOTH-09, BOTH-16, GEO-01, GEO-02, GEO-17, GEO-20) sit in both the search registry and the AI-readiness registry with different labels and different weights, and the audit agent is instructed to return every id from both registries. The pipeline then runs the gap computation once per registry, so one real defect emits two cards. Priority is derived purely from (1 − score) × registry weight, and the weights differ between the two registries, so the two cards get different chips for the identical underlying defect: at a full fail, the sitemap check is important on one side and moderate on the other; the freshness check is important on one side and urgent on the other; the scannable-sections check is urgent on one side and moderate on the other. A client cannot trust a priority system that grades the same problem two ways on the same screen.

src/lib/intel/seo-geo.ts:225-238 — audit prompt: "Every check id from both registries MUST appear exactly once in the JSON"

In src/lib/intel/seo-geo.ts:772-776, after concatenating the two computeCheckGaps results, collapse gaps sharing `id.split(":")[0]`, keeping the higher scoreLift and promoting the survivor's lever to "BOTH" where the registries disagree. title: The "Search engines" filter files four search checks under "AI answers" instead
surface: Client dashboard → Search & AI visibility → "What we're fixing" → "Search engines" tab (/clients/[id])
whatYouSee: Click "Search engines" expecting your search problems. Four of the seventeen search checks are missing — including whether your site blocks Google's crawler, whether each page has exactly one main headline, whether your update dates are genuine, and whether your pages open with a short summary. They only appear under "AI answers".
whyItsWrong: The channel is derived from the rec-id prefix rather than from the registry the check came from. GEO-01, GEO-02, GEO-17 and GEO-20 are entries in the search-score registry (eligibility, on-page, structure buckets), but their ids begin with GEO, so the lever comes out as AI-only, the presenter maps that to the AI channel, and the filter drops them from the search tab. A filter that quietly moves rows to the wrong tab makes the client believe a category is clean when it isn't.
